fix.rule: each declared output PATTERN contributes its newest match; the MINIMUM is taken ACROSS patterns
deliberately_preserved: One pattern contributes one artifact; the minimum is never taken across every file on disk, so a superseded Cerebro export the owner never deleted does not mark stage 4 stale for ever.
artifact now names the OLDEST output - the file the owner must look at. Naming the fresh sibling sent them to a file that was fine.
Equal mtimes are READY, not STALE. Strict '<'. An engine writing inside one clock tick of its input is the normal fast case; a permanent false STALE is worse. Pinned in revision 2.
fix.docstring_updated: The module's staleness rule read 'output mtime < input mtime', the exact ambiguity that permitted the defect. It now reads 'OLDEST output mtime < newest input mtime' and says why.

defect_1.defect: Each asserted argv == ['--seed', seed] AND assertNotIn('PWNED', run.stdout) in the same body. Four corpus seeds contain PWNED literally, so a CORRECT renderer is exactly what makes the marker appear in the probe's argv echo. The two assertions could never both hold on any machine.

defect_1.fix: Assert the property actually meant: the probe prints exactly ONE line, so a second line is output PowerShell produced on its own. defect_2.severity: real product defect, same class as DEFECT A -- a wrong value presented as a right one
defect_2.masked_by: defect_1, which aborted the seed loop at index 2 before it reached this seed at index 3
defect_2.defect: _ps_quote renders nurse"quote" as 'nurse"quote"'; PowerShell 5.1 rebuilds the native command line without escaping the embedded quote and the C runtime reads it as a delimiter. The child receives nursequote. The owner would have searched a keyword they never typed, with nothing on screen to show it.

measured_renderings.note: byte-exact -- so this value IS renderable

defect_2.resolution: REFUSED at the CLI boundary, as a third entry in unsupported_value(). Exit 2, structured UNSUPPORTED_VALUE, next_command null, no engine command in text mode -- verified end-to-end through the real shell.
defect_2.refusal_is_a_choice_not_an_impossibility: Unlike the trailing backslash, this value can be rendered exactly. Emitting it means carrying the C runtime's backslash-doubling rules inside a renderer whose job is a two-word keyword, each rule needing its own Windows proof. A double quote is not part of any real Amazon search term. The docstrings state this explicitly: a refusal claiming an impossibility it has not got would be the same overstatement this document has corrected twice.
defect_2.owner_decision: Taken explicitly by the owner on 2026-08-01, presented against the alternative of escaping. Recorded so it can be reversed the same way.
defect_2.corpus_change: DOUBLE_QUOTE_SEED moved out of ADVERSARIAL_SEEDS and pinned out of it by name beside TRAILING_BACKSLASH_SEED. A refused value inside the gate corpus fails the gate for a limitation the renderer is not allowed to fix.
defect_2.single_quote_unaffected: nurse's gift still renders 'nurse''s gift' and is still supported. The refusal is exactly as wide as the character.

defects.defect: In PowerShell a line whose FIRST token is a quoted string is a string EXPRESSION, not a command. _ps_quote(sys.executable) quotes any interpreter path containing a space, e.g. C:\Program Files\Python311\python.exe.
defects.consequence: The generated .ps1 would have ECHOED the path, exited 0, and json.loads would have raised on the echoed text. The gate test would have failed on the environment rather than on the renderer, presenting as a JSONDecodeError that reads like a broken test.
defects.why_undetected: The Windows-only test cannot run on this macOS clone, so nothing here would ever have exercised it. It would have failed on the first Windows machine whose Python lives under C:\Program Files.

defects.defect: Windows PowerShell 5.1 reads a BOM-less .ps1 as the system ANSI code page.
defects.consequence: The Unicode seed added for this review would have been mojibaked before PowerShell parsed it; the test would have measured file encoding.

defects.defect: Python stdout falls back to the ANSI code page when REDIRECTED rather than attached to a console -- exactly what Tee-Object does.
defects.consequence: A non-ASCII seed raises UnicodeEncodeError and aborts the capture.

self_correction.stays_out_of_execution_corpus: It is a PowerShell native-marshalling limitation BELOW the renderer. Failing the acceptance gate on something _ps_quote cannot fix would be wrong.

prewindows_review_disposition.policy_adopted: Do not knowingly run a deterministic defective gate. A concrete, reproducible defect found before the environment run may be fixed with a focused test and a branch-only commit. Do not continue speculative refactoring once no known blocker remains.

reversal.my_previous_position: Document it as a PowerShell native-marshalling limitation below the renderer and exclude it from the execution corpus.
reversal.why: Calling it a shell limitation does not remove it from the paste-safety contract. A value that looks supported and arrives at the engine changed is exactly the failure class this work exists to close.
reversal.decision: Option B - reject with a structured error and test the refusal.
reversal.implementation: unsupported_value() refuses a value that BOTH requires quoting AND ends in a backslash. Exit 2, no command emitted, structured UNSUPPORTED_VALUE in --json with next_command null.
reversal.refusal_is_exactly_as_wide_as_the_defect: A bare 'nurse\' needs no quoting, so there is no quote for the C runtime to mis-parse, and it stays SUPPORTED (exit 0). Only the quote-required form is refused.

holes_the_contracts_found_in_my_own_fixe.hole: The Windows test used sys.executable, which may or may not contain a space on any given machine, so the `&` fix could have passed without ever being exercised.
holes_the_contracts_found_in_my_own_fixe.class: Same as the D2 skipped-test gate: a check that can silently not check.
holes_the_contracts_found_in_my_own_fixe.fix: test_a_quoted_executable_needs_the_call_operator_to_run_at_all uses a CONTROLLED fixture under 'dir with space' and asserts BOTH directions - without `&` PowerShell echoes the path, with `&` it runs. A test that only checked the fix would never show the hazard is real.

holes_the_contracts_found_in_my_own_fixe.hole: I fixed the redirected-stdout encoding trap in the capture script and LEFT IT LIVE IN THE TEST. The argv probe used print(), and its stdout there is a pipe, so on Windows the non-ASCII seed would have raised UnicodeEncodeError inside the probe and the failure would have read as a renderer defect.
holes_the_contracts_found_in_my_own_fixe.fix: The probe encodes UTF-8 bytes itself, independent of the environment it is measured in.

authoritative_encoding_mechanism.why: UTF-8 mode also changes the FILESYSTEM encoding, and this tool's entire job is reading filenames. Changing how they decode would alter the measurement. Narrower is correct: stdio only. Per the review's caution against stacking overrides, this is the only encoding override set.

table_invariants_added: test_no_two_declared_outputs_of_a_stage_can_match_the_same_file - required-all is defeated if one artifact fills two slots, which the _resolve overlap guard does not cover

test_every_command_starts_with_a_bare_literal_token - this is WHY no printed command needs '&'. The production contract is satisfied structurally rather than by adding noise to every printed line, and the test is the tripwire if a template ever leads with a substituted value.

required_checks_audit.premise: The rev-5 review returned stop_coding_now: true and remaining_known_static_defects: NONE_IDENTIFIED_FROM_THE_SUMMARY. That last phrase is load-bearing -- it was identified FROM THE SUMMARY. Auditing the SOURCE against each required_checks list found six that were not met. Every one maps to an explicit check; none is speculative refactoring.

gaps.required_by: reversal_review: 'the predicate is derived from the actual renderer behavior rather than from a separate approximation'
gaps.gap: needs_quoting() re-wrote _ps_quote's bare-safe condition instead of being the one the renderer calls.
gaps.risk: Change what renders bare and the refusal silently stops describing the behaviour it exists to describe.

gaps.required_by: reversal_review: 'the accepted bare-safe trailing-backslash value round-trips exactly on Windows'
gaps.gap: 'nurse\\' -- the value the tool explicitly CLAIMS to support -- was absent from the Windows corpus.
gaps.risk: A claim of support that is never executed is the same untested assertion this work keeps finding.
gaps.fix: Added to ADVERSARIAL_SEEDS. If PowerShell mangles it after all, the claim is wrong and the refusal must widen; the corpus is how that gets found.

gaps.required_by: control_character_policy: 'before command rendering, workspace lookup, and subprocess creation'
gaps.risk: A path with a control character was reported 'workspace not found' -- true but useless, sending the owner to look for a missing directory instead of at the character they pasted.
gaps.fix: Validation moved first; it touches no filesystem so nothing is lost. Verified.

gaps.required_by: absolute_side_effect_snapshot: 'canonical paths and hashes, not names alone'
gaps.risk: Misses a file MODIFIED rather than created, and collapses same-named files in different directories -- a redirect that OVERWROTE the probe read as no side effect at all.
gaps.fix: Relative path -> content hash, snapshotted per iteration after the .ps1 is written, so the deliberately-changing script file need not be excluded.

gaps.required_by: required_output_uniqueness: 'Windows case-insensitive path equivalence is accounted for'
gaps.risk: PRODUCT-PAGE.json and product-page.json are one file on Windows.

gaps.gap: Every printed command begins with bare `python` -- which is WHY none needs a call operator -- but bare `python` is a PATH lookup and was never verified.
gaps.risk: On Windows it can resolve to the Microsoft Store alias stub under WindowsApps, which OPENS THE STORE rather than running Python, or to an interpreter without this repository's dependencies. The printed command is only as good as what that name resolves to.
gaps.fix: The capture resolves it, refuses the Store alias by path, proves it can import core.pipeline_status from the repo, and records path and version.

also_closed: The H1 fixture asserts its path actually contains a space, not only that it needs quoting
Invoke-Capture exposes Output and LineCount; stdout and stderr are merged ON PURPOSE because their interleaving is what makes a failure readable
A non-empty but IRRELEVANT runs/T2 is recorded as not exercising stages 5 and 11 rather than passing as evidence for them
PYTHONIOENCODING process scope documented: it dies with the script and cannot leak into a later shell

my_own_guards_that_failed_and_were_right.why_it_failed: It collected EVERY `for x in name` loop, so the new tree snapshot's `for f in files` counted as a rival corpus.
It asserted every corpus seed comes back single-quoted, which the deliberately BARE 'nurse\\' breaks.
my_own_guards_that_failed_and_were_right.fix: Asserts ROUND-TRIP through the renderer's own inverse -- the property that actually matters, and one that does not block adding a legitimately bare case.
my_own_guards_that_failed_and_were_right.lesson: A test that has to be relaxed to admit a true case was asserting the wrong thing.

ambiguity_resolved.resolution: The reviewer's reading is correct. NO production next-command starts with '&', because none starts with a quoted value. The '& ' assertion applies only to the controlled Windows fixture, which deliberately invokes a quoted path under 'dir with space' to prove the hazard is real. The report previously listed both facts without distinguishing them and now carries an explicit scope note.
ambiguity_resolved.tripwire: test_every_command_starts_with_a_bare_literal_token fails if a template ever leads with a substituted value, at which point the renderer must emit '&'.
